title: Tenali Raman Tale 120

full_text:
During a severe drought that impoverished thousands of cattle herders in the countryside, the chief court priests persuaded King Krishnadevaraya to perform a lavish expiation ritual:
'Maharaj, to bring rain and cleanse the sins of the realm, you must cast a life-size sacred cow in solid gold, weighing one hundred tolas, and donate it exclusively to the senior priests of the council!'

The King, in his devout anxiety, was preparing to melt treasury gold when Tenali Raman arrived.
Tenali said: 'Maharaj, donating a golden cow is a noble thought. But let us invite the poorest cowherds of the kingdom to witness the sacred donation.'

On the day of the ceremony, the magnificent golden cow stood upon the altar, gleaming with fifty thousand gold coins' worth of precious metal.
The priests stood ready with silver platters to claim the treasure.

Tenali Raman entered the temple leading an emaciated, starving, living mother cow and her hungry little calf, whose ribs were poking through their hides.
Tenali led the starving animals straight up to the altar.

The priests shouted in disgust:
'Tenali! What sacrilege is this? Taking a filthy, starving cow onto the sacred altar of the Golden Cow?'

Tenali turned to the King and the priests with fierce, righteous moral clarity:
'Sacrilege?
Look at these two cows!
This living cow was created by heaven; she gave milk to nourish your children, and her bullocks plowed your fields for twenty years!
Today, because of the drought, she and her calf are starving to death, while her owner weeps without bread!
And here you stand, casting one hundred tolas of pure gold into a cold, dead, metal idol that cannot eat, cannot produce a single drop of milk, and cannot plow a field, merely to divide the gold among yourselves!

Tell me, O priests: which cow is truly sacred to heaven?
The living cow whose stomach cries for grass, or the dead metal cow that feeds only your greed?
If you melt this golden cow, its gold could buy grain and fodder to feed ten thousand starving cattle and poor farmers across the entire province for an entire year!'

Tenali’s profound, prophetic words struck the assembly like a thunderbolt.
Worshippers wept openly, and the priests lowered their heads in utter shame.
King Krishnadevaraya stood up, his eyes filled with tears of awakening:
'Tenali has spoken the truth of heaven!'

The King canceled the golden donation on the spot.
He ordered the gold melted and converted into emergency fodder banks, grain subsidies, and drinking water tanks for the drought-stricken pastoral communities.
The living cow and calf were adopted into the royal dairy, and Tenali was blessed by thousands of grateful farmers as the true protector of life.
moral: Religious charity is fulfilled by feeding living mouths, not by casting golden idols to enrich priests.
